prompts.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / coherent pixel-art floor production master.
Reference image: the attached pixel floor is the ONE AND ONLY exact style and color reference. Keep the same blue-grey steel value ramp, muted brass, crisp pixel clusters, sparse wear and regular64nativepixel panel pitch. No other realistic or photographic material reference is allowed.
Produce ONE single CONNECTED 2-by-2-cell FLOOR SECTION, not four separate sprites, not a display sheet and not a framed island. Conceptually the whole artwork is256x256 nativepixels. Each half-sized cell is128x128. Interior panel pattern: FOUR BY FOUR large steel plates across the whole square, each plate64x64 conceptualpixels. Principal panel joints at x64,128,192 and y64,128,192. Pixel shading3-4 controlled value steps per surface, small complete brass fittings inside the plate corners. No overall top-to-bottom lighting gradient or different colors in different quadrants.
This connected section has an exterior perimeter ONLY on the NORTH and WEST sides. Place a continuous8conceptualpixel complete-profile north beam along y0..7 and equal-width west beam along x0..7. At NW they meet as a clean SQUARE pixel-art manufactured corner, completely solid, with matching layered metal profile. No bevel cutout or pretend dark transparent background at that square corner.
IMPORTANT: East and south boundaries are OPEN CUT-THROUGH FLOOR CONTINUATIONS. Absolutely no raised beam, outer frame, endcap, closure line, drop shadow or border decoration along the right or bottom canvas edge. The floor continues beyond those two cuts. The north beam reaches the right image boundary with its continuous cross-section. The west beam reaches the bottom image boundary with its continuous cross-section.
The four quadrants are therefore: top-left NW exterior corner; top-right north straight edge; bottom-left west straight edge; bottom-right full center. They are a SINGLE connected floor surface, with physical panel seams and colors continuing through the two half-image cut lines. Do not draw artificial tile divider/grid overlay or labels. This is artwork for later cutting into four whole tiles, and alignment/continuity matters more than decorative detail.
Completely fill the whole square canvas with opaque floor artwork, RGB or solid PNG. No page margins or transparent gutters. No smoothing, gradients, photorealistic grit, dense noise, fancy shiny3D highlights, different color grading, text, watermark, separate panels or additional items. Use restrained palette and pixel contours matching the attached pixel reference, not a new interpretation.

Use case: style-transfer
Asset type: ONE continuous opaque north-south industrial floor corridor master image for three vertically adjacent game tiles.
Primary request: Create a single seamless manufactured corridor using ONLY the attached new pixel floor image as the exact color and pixel-art style reference. This must be ONE intact connected rectangular floor, not three separate sprites or a presentation sheet. Keep the reference's muted blue-grey steel, dark blue edging, compact readable pixel clusters, and restrained brass. Do not invent a different brighter, darker, greener, or more realistic material for any part of the corridor.
Input image: the attached floor_center_pixel_v001.png is the ONLY art reference. Match its color family and pixel shading language directly. It shows four large plates; use the same plate scale and industrial pixel-cluster construction. Do not use any old realistic references.
Canvas: exact tall PORTRAIT 1:3 aspect ratio, preferably 1024px wide by 3072px high. The conceptual native grid is 128px wide by 384px high, enlarged uniformly. Fill the canvas EDGE TO EDGE with the corridor floor. No surrounding page or display margin. The floor is FULL WIDTH and completely opaque, including its edges and four corners. No transparent pixels, fake transparency, cut-outs, black backdrop around the object, cast shadows outside the object, or inset floating panel.
Shared geometry: this whole 128x384 conceptual corridor has continuous vertical side beams exactly 8 conceptual pixels wide, x=0..7 and x=120..127. They run uninterrupted from the top boundary to the bottom boundary. The extreme top has a closed horizontal metal end beam at y=0..7; the extreme bottom has a closed horizontal metal end beam at y=376..383. Square pixel metal corner joins are correct. There are NO other transverse end beams and NO internal caps at y=128 or y=256.
Shared floor plate rhythm: TWO columns by SIX rows of large steel plates across the entire corridor. A thin ordinary vertical plate joint lies at conceptual x=64. Thin ordinary horizontal plate joints follow the same 64px cadence: y=64,128,192,256,320. These are subtle panel joints, not thick beams or closing barriers. Each 128px-high conceptual tile thus has the same 2x2 plate scale. All neighboring plates share the exact same local palette and shading levels. Keep panel texture sparse and coarse enough to read as deliberate pixel clusters; avoid photorealistic speckle, small noisy wear, or smooth rendered surfaces.
Tile extraction intention: the upper conceptual 128x128 section will be the NORTH closed end tile, the middle 128x128 section the NS-through corridor, and the lower 128x128 section the SOUTH closed end tile. Their contacts are already drawn continuously in this one master. Do NOT frame those three sections separately. Do NOT insert any gutter, gap, outer frame, shadow strip, or stylistic transition between them. Do NOT draw a transverse closing cap in the middle section.
Lighting and palette: copy the reference's muted blue-grey values closely, with only a few flat pixel shading levels and tiny restrained brass fasteners. Small upper-left highlights on metal edges are fine. NO overall top-to-bottom or left-to-right lighting gradient; NO different hue, brightness, weathering density, or shading treatment in the upper, middle and lower thirds. Do not rotate or mirror the reference to construct end sections. Use the same art treatment throughout.
Style: crisp pixel art with connected color clusters, axis-aligned pixels, clean readable outlines and spare metal detail. Preserve the final 128px tile resolution, not a 32px final texture. No arbitrary fixed 16-color limit.
Constraints: Exactly ONE long connected complete corridor occupying the full 1:3 portrait canvas. Actual opaque floor background. No labels, tile grid overlay, typography, watermark, preview panels, separate parts, perspective, isometric view, camera angle, blur, antialiasing haze, realistic grain, water, rivet posts outside the frame, or a page margin.

Edit the FIRST reference image, a continuous blue-gray industrial metal corridor mother, into a corrected reusable PIXEL ART corridor. Use the SECOND reference only as the exact material, colors, bevel contrast, gold bolt and pixel-cluster style reference: this is the matching large floor it must connect to. Preserve the dark blue-gray scratched steel palette and crisp stepped square pixel marks. Do not add a different lighting treatment, realistic shading, global gradient, softer brush marks, vignette or new hue. Colors of the plate interiors and seam highlights should match the second reference.

Render ONE continuous tall rectangular top-down metal surface, edge to edge, no background, no margins, no transparency, no montage or contact sheet. Keep EXACT portrait ratio 1:3. Think of this whole image as a 128 by 384 pixel mother that will later be cut into three 128 by 128 square tiles at one third and two thirds of the height. Do not outline or separate the three tiles.

Structural correction:
- The old side rails are too thin. Replace them with clearly visible solid connected metal beams spanning the FULL height on both left and right edges, EACH exactly 1/16 of total image width (8px at conceptual128). Same broad double bevel dark-blue metal rim and pale blue-grey highlight as the second reference. Keep the overall floor solid across its full width.
- The very top and bottom ends have matching closed horizontal beams with gold bolts. Each is 8px tall in conceptual pixels. Square pixel corner joins connect to the full-width side beams; no chamfer, detached fragments, rounded edge or outside background.
- The steel has TWO columns and SIX rows on a strict modular grid. Main interior vertical seam at half of the full image width. Five internal horizontal seams placed at exactly 1/6, 2/6, 3/6, 4/6 and 5/6 of TOTAL image height, corresponding to conceptual y=64,128,192,256,320. The tile cuts are y128 and y256. Beams lie INSIDE the original grid; do not inset and then divide the remaining interior into six equal rows. That mistaken inset subdivision was causing cumulative drift.
- At one-third and two-thirds height a shared horizontal plate joint continues exactly through the cut. The top and bottom rims are only at the total mother endpoints; no crossbar endcap at the tile cuts.
- Six plate rows have equal 64px pitch. Their scratches can vary in coherent coarse pixel clusters, but do not rotate, resize, stagger or curve the board grid.
- 2px conceptual plate bevels, small matching golden square bolts at plate corners. Sharp nearest-neighbor looking clusters, no blur and no antialiasing.

Output only this one continuous 1:3 opaque corridor mother. It must look cut from the same industrial pixel floor as the second reference. No text, guides, labels, grid overlay, colored markers, shadows outside the material or extra assets.
